title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is the end of a letter from Pierre Deligne to Grothendieck, signed 'Pierre' and addressed 'Cher Schnik' on the previous page, dated 27/3/81. It answers Grothendieck's questions on profinite completions, Galois groups and the Teichmüller (mapping class) group, all relevant to the anabelian / Teichmüller-tower programme.

(1) Claim: every open subgroup G_K of G_Q = Gal(Qbar/Q), with K/Q finite, has trivial centre. Deligne says this follows, as for free profinite groups (previous page), from class field theory.
- Reduction: suppose z ≠ 1 is central in G_K. Take an open normal U ⊂ G_K with z ∉ U. Let K' be the fixed field of the closed subgroup generated by U and z, and L the fixed field of U. Then K'/K is finite and L/K' is cyclic, generated by the image σ of z. Also z stays central in G_{K'}.
- Conjugation by z acts on G_L^ab = Gal(L^ab/L) through σ (functoriality of the reciprocity map).
- Gal(L^ab/L) ≅ π_0(C_L), the profinite completion of the idele class group modulo its connected component. σ acts nontrivially on it, contradicting centrality.
- Explicit witness: take a prime p of K' splitting completely in L as p_1…p_g. There is an abelian extension of L ramified at one p_i and not at the others (class field theory, e.g. via ray class fields). Since Gal(L/K') permutes the p_i transitively, σ moves the corresponding inertia subgroup, so it cannot act trivially.

(2) Nielsen realization. Every finite subgroup of the Teichmüller modular group (mapping class group) is realized as a group of automorphisms of some Riemann surface. Deligne recalls a proof idea in the style of É. Cartan: a natural (Finsler) metric making Teichmüller space 'negatively curved', so any compact group of isometries has a fixed point. A marginal note records the reference Poenaru gave: Kerckhoff, Bull. AMS, using Teichmüller theory as revisited by Thurston.

(3) Personal paragraph in Russian. Deligne has been married since September; Lena arrived in Brussels on 3 March; everything is new for her; she said 'nothing is automatic; I always have to think; it is very interesting, but sometimes I get tired'. The letter closes.
errors: Deligne's recollection of the Nielsen-realization proof is inaccurate. Kerckhoff (announcement Bull. AMS 2 (1980); full proof Annals 1983) used convexity of hyperbolic length functions along Thurston earthquake paths, not a negatively curved Finsler metric. Masur (1975) showed the Teichmüller metric is not negatively curved in Busemann's sense. A Cartan-type fixed-point argument was realized later for the Weil–Petersson metric (Wolpert), and via the CAT(0) Weil–Petersson completion.

The centre-freeness argument tacitly needs the reduction to K' and L/K' cyclic generated by the image of z (z replaced into a cyclic quotient). This is implicit in 'pour L/K cyclique de générateur σ' and in the reduction of the previous page; it is correct.
Minor: Gal(L^ab/L) ≅ π_0(C_L) holds via the reciprocity map with profinite completion understood. For number fields π_0(C_L) is already profinite, so this is fine.

ideas.what: Open subgroups of G_Q (absolute Galois groups of number fields) have trivial centre, proved via class field theory: the Galois action on idele classes / localized ramification is nontrivial
ideas.modern_name: Centre-freeness of absolute Galois groups of number fields (cf. Neukirch–Schmidt–Wingberg, Cohomology of Number Fields, Ch. XII)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore/Neukirch school (1960s–70s); standard input in anabelian geometry
ideas.where_published: Implicitly used in Esquisse d'un programme / the letter to Faltings context; not proved there

ideas.what: Free profinite groups (profinite completions of free groups) have no torsion and trivial centre (previous page, continued here)
ideas.modern_name: Torsion-freeness and centre-freeness of free profinite groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (Serre, Cohomologie galoisienne; Lubotzky–van den Dries etc.)

ideas.what: Finite subgroups of the mapping class group are realized by automorphism groups of Riemann surfaces; idea of a fixed point via nonpositive curvature (Cartan)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kerckhoff 1980/1983 (also Wolpert via Weil–Petersson convexity; earlier Fenchel/Nielsen for cyclic and solvable groups)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme uses finite subgroups of Teichmüller modular groups / automorphisms of curves in the Teichmüller tower discussion

deep.surprise_reason: This is a letter from Deligne relaying standard facts: centre-freeness of Galois groups of number fields via class field theory, and Nielsen realization with Kerckhoff's reference. It is of historical interest as documentation of the Deligne–Grothendieck exchange during the 'Teichmülleries' period, but it contains no new or uncredited mathematics.
transcription_corrections: The author is Pierre Deligne (signature 'Pierre'), not Grothendieck; this is a letter addressed to Grothendieck ('Schnik').
'Kerchof' in the margin should be read as Kerckhoff (S. Kerckhoff, 'The Nielsen realization problem', Bull. AMS 2 (1980)).
Russian line: 'Я женатой [?] с сентября' is more plausibly 'Я женат с сентября' ('I have been married since September').
'в Брюсселе' — Deligne's spelling, meaning 'in Brussels' (standard Russian: в Брюсселе).
'Teichmuller' should read Teichmüller throughout; 'pour une métrique (finslérienne) naturelle convenable' with the struck word removed.
